newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan expects island talks with Japan next month.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan expects island talks with Japan next month.

text.p: Taiwan's Foreign Ministry said on Tuesday that it expected to hold a second round of talks with Japan in early October to discuss fishing rights in waters near a disputed chain of East China Sea islands.

"The Japanese side should have a formal response very soon," Vice Foreign Minister Cheng Chien-jen said on state television. "We should be able to have a second round of dialogue in early October concerning fishing rights."
Cheng's comments marked the first time that Taipei, which has no diplomatic ties with Tokyo, has mentioned a timetable for talks to resolve the increasingly bitter dispute.

Initial talks were held in August when Japanese officials came to Taiwan after Japanese rightists erected a lighthouse on one of the uninhabited East China Sea islands, triggering a sovereignty dispute.
Taiwan, China and Japan all claim the islands, called the Diaoyus in Chinese and the Senkakus in Japanese.

Although Japan reportedly agreed during the August talks to halt plans to further assert Tokyo's claim, the row escalated in recent weeks after Japanese patrol boats repelled several private Taiwanese vessels nearing the islands.
